4.6       On the perusal of the list, the Committee notes that most of the erring employees fall in the category of Para-
medical staff (class-III/IV)  i.e. Safai Karamchari or Nursing Attendants etc. It seems that no complaints have been
received by the authorities in respect of other categories of staff which the Committee is not inclined to believe. The
Committee feels that majority of staff  in  the hospital are not properly oriented towards their duties.   The Committee,
therefore, recommends that inservice training with special focus on work culture and approach towards patients may be
conducted on regular basis for them.
V.        DR.  RAM  MANOHAR  LOHIA  HOSPITAL
5.1
              Plan  allocation for Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi in  BE 2001-2002  was Rs.21.00 crores which
has been decreased to Rs.17.20 crores in 2002-2003. Explaining  the decrease in allocation, the Department has
informed that Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital has procured MRI System costing around Rs.7.00 crores during the
year 2001-2002.   Since the hospital has no such project for the year 2002-2003, the plan allocation has been reduced for
the year 2002-2003.
5.2
       The Project for establishing a Trauma Centre at the  Hospital has remained at the proposal stage for a
considerable period.   The Expenditure Finance Committee at its meeting held on 1st June, 2001 has finally approved the
proposal.   Administrative approval and expenditure sanction to the proposal was subsequently issued on the 25 th July,
2001.  The drawings of the project have been submitted to the appropriate civic authorities for their necessary approval. 
The Minister for Health and Family Welfare laid the foundation stone on 31st December, 2001.
5.3       The Committee is happy to note that some progress has been made in this regard during 2001-02 and   finally the
project has started taking shape. However, the Committee is of the opinion that  given the increase in number of road
accidents every year in Delhi and also considerable time taken in getting the EFC proposal, the Department should make
concerted efforts to get the Trauma Centre established within the  fixed time frame i.e. upto 31.3.2004.
VI.       CENTRAL  INSTITUTE OF PSYCHIATRY,  RANCHI
6.1
        The Plan  allocation for the Central Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi in BE 2001-2002 was Rs.7.00 crores which
was drastically reduced to Rs.2.50 crores at the RE stage. Plan allocation for 2002-03 is Rs. 3.50 crores against the
projected demand of Rs. 8.30 crores made by the Institute.  On being asked to specify the reasons for drastic cut made
in  the allocation, the Department has clarified that the Plan budget of the Department of Health was reduced by Rs.104
crores at RE stage which   had to be apportioned amongst the Institutes and Programmes. The amount of Rs.4.80 crores
for purchase of equipments for the Institute  was sanctioned only in December, 2001, by which time the RE had been
decided and allocation of the Institute was cut due to low expenditure upto that date. 
6.2       The exercise of purchasing the required equipments for the Institute has been continuing for a considerable
period of time.   The Committee has been informed that the amount of Rs. 4.80 crores for purchasing equipments was
sanctioned in December, 2001.   The Committee is, however, constrained to observe that the formal letter conveying the
approval of the Competent Authority in this regard could be issued only on 19
th February, 2002.   It is understood that at
that time the Institute was having an unspent balance of Rs. 3,01,76,510 against which some of the equipments out of
the sanctioned equipments could have been purchased during 2001-02 itself.  The Committee apprehends that this
amount could not have been utilized for want of completion of procedural formalities.   This becomes clear from the
request of the Institute  for increased allocation of  Rs. 8.30 crores for meeting the  expenditure towards purchase of
equipments amounting to Rs. 4.80 crores.   It seems that the Institute will have to wait upto the RE stage as the
allocation of only Rs. 3.50 crores has been made for 2002-03.   The Committee is deeply anguished at this state of
affairs. The Committee, strongly recommends that the Department should suitably enhance the allocation of CIP,
Ranchi so that these equipments which are essential to meet the needs of the patients can be procured at the earliest.
6.2
        The Department has further informed  that a proposal for creation/recreation  of 41 posts at the Central Institute
of Psychiatry based on the reports of the two Study Groups (one under the Chairmanship of Smt. Sunila Basant, then
Joint Secretary in the Ministry and another Expert Group from NIMHANS, Bangalore) has been under the consideration
of DGHS.  Out of these 41 posts, Directorate General recommended for creation of only 24 posts, which are primarily
required for augmenting the Institute.  It was  also indicated by the Ministry  that 13 posts could be abolished to find
some savings towards creation of the 24 posts, the expenditure for which after abolition of 13 posts was computed at
Rs.38.00 lakhs per annum.  The proposal was forwarded to the Department of Expenditure on 17.7.2001, which sought
some additional information in a statement showing cases handled in the last 10 years, posts sanctioned in various

116th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/116threport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:24]
grades and in existence, number of posts now to be created discipline-wise.  The said information has been sent to the
Department of Expenditure through the Internal Finance in  January, 2002 for their approval and the approval is
awaited.
6.4       The issue  of creation of required posts for CIP, Ranchi started with an IWSU study conducted as early as in 
1997.  Thereafter, another study was conducted by NIMHANS IN 2000.   Final outcome has been that out of the
proposal for creation/recreation of 41 posts, only 24 posts have been recommended for creation by DGHS.
6.5       On a specific query about the scaling down of number of proposed posts, the Department has clarified that
austerity  measures and the ban on creation/revival /filling up of posts led to revision of the proposal.   The Committee
expresses its serious reservations on this development.  What is more shocking is that as a bargain for creating these 24
posts, the Ministry has wished for abolishing 13 existing posts.
6.6       The Committee strongly feels that the position is very bad in CIP, Ranchi.   Creation of required posts apart,
even sanctioned posts are not filled up.    Out of 19 teaching  posts of Associate/Assistant/Professor, only 6 are filled
up.   Similarly, out of 24 non-teaching posts, only 9 are in position.   The Committee is of the view that drastic steps
need to be taken by all the concerned authorities so that the Central Institute  of Psychiatry, Ranchi  can provide the
services in the area of mental health care which is very much required in the present scenario.
VII.      ALL INDIA INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES (AIIMS)
7.1
               All India Institute of Medical Sciences was established in 1956 by an Act of Parliament as an institution of
national importance .  AIIMS is conceived to be a Centre of excellence in modern medicine with comprehensive
training facility.
7.2
              Plan allocation for the All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi was Rs.100.00 crores for BE 2001-
2002 which was reduced to Rs.95.00 crores at the RE stage.  However, plan allocation for 2002-2003 has been stepped
up to Rs.105.00 crores.  On being asked about the reasons for reduction in RE 2001-2002, the Department has replied
that the cut was effected because of reduction in the overall plan ceiling of the Department.  The Department has also
informed that AIIMS has asked for an allocation of Rs.124.46 crores for 2002-2003 but keeping in view the pace of
expenditure during the Ninth Plan, a plan ceiling of Rs.105.00 crores has been fixed for AIIMS for the year 2002-2003.
7.3
       The Committee notes that plan allocation of Rs.100.00 crores in BE 2001-2002 was meant for creation of
additional wards, labs and ICUs at Cardiothoracic and Neurosciences Centre for equipping the organ retrieval bank  and
for starting work on the Apex Trauma Care Centre. The Committee fails to understand as to how with the cut in
allocation at the revised stage in 2001-2002, the proposed work in AIIMS as mentioned above would have been
completed.  The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress made in this regard.
7.4       The Committee has been informed that the proposal for setting up of an Apex Centre for Trauma Care at AIIMS
has been approved at an estimated cost of Rs. 54.14 crores.  The Centre would be multi-disciplinary, which apart from
providing holistic Trauma Care Services would also be used as a role model for other Trauma Centres in terms of
conceptualization, project formulation and operation.  The construction work entrusted to HSCC, New Delhi, has started
in the month of January, 2002,  and is expected to be completed by January, 2003.  The Committee is happy to note that
the work of establishing Trauma Centre at AIIMS  has finally begun and hopes that  it would be completed by the target
date.
VIII.     POST GRAUDATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH, CHANDIGARH
8.1
       Plan allocation for PGIMER, Chandigarh was Rs.45.00 crores in BE 2001-2002, which was substantially reduced
to Rs.25.00 crores at the RE stage and the same allocation has been made for the year 2002-2003.  Explaining the
reasons for such a drastic cut in allocation, the Department has informed that during 2001-2002 under plan, the
PGIMER, Chandigarh had proposed to complete the ongoing schemes of Advanced Paediatric Centre Phase—II and
National Institute of Nursing Education.  Besides, it had proposed to take up the construction activities of Advanced

earlier, approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) in July, 2000.  The Institute had also planned
to purchase equipments for new projects.  However, only the construction activities of Bone Marrow Transplant Centre,
Advanced Paediatric Centre, Phase—II and Advanced Eye Centre could progress.  The standing committees were
dissolved in July, 2001 and reconstituted in October, 2001.  Finally, the Standing Estate Committee under the
Chairmanship of Secretary (H) met on 24
th January, 2002 and a large number of construction activities were granted

be stated for want of administrative approval although required funds were allocated at the beginning of the year.   In

XII.      NATIONAL  MALARIA  ERADICATION  PROGRAMME
12.1
          National Malaria Eradication Programme is a category II Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 50.50 Cost sharing
basis between the Centre and State Governments.  The Central Government on its part provides drugs, insecticides and
larvicides etc.  The State Governments meet the operational cost including salary of the staff, except North Eastern
States, which are being provided 100% Central assistance under the programme since December, 1994. 
12.2
          The Plan allocation for National Anti Malaria Programme in BE 2001-02 was Rs.168.00 crores which was
increased to Rs.173.00 crores at the RE stage.  Plan allocation for 2002-2003 has been further increased to Rs.187.00
crores, additional allocation meant for construction of two new buildings, one each for Directorate of the National Anti-
Malaria Programme and Malaria Research Centre under ICMR. 
12.3     The Committee observes that during the Ninth Plan, funds allocated for this Programme have invariably
remained under-utilised.  During 2000-01, BE allocation of Rs. 255.00 crores had to be reduced to Rs. 194.00 crores at
the RE stage and actual expenditure incurred was Rs. 188.32 crores.   Although BE allocation  of Rs. 168.00 crores in 
BE  2001-02 was enhanced to Rs. 173.00 crores at RE stage,  expenditure reported upto  February, 2002 is only
Rs.116.92 crores.  Seeing the trend in earlier years, the Committee is not inclined to  believe the Department’s
contention that the balance  amount  will be utilized during the remaining part of the financial year.
12.4     World Bank assisted Enhanced  Malaria Control Project is operative from 30
th September, 1997 for a period of
five years in 100 districts in eight States of Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhatisgarh,
Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Orissa.   The Committee observes that utilization position of funds under this Programme is
very poor as all the District Malaria Control Societies are having varying amount of unspent balance with them as on
30.4.2001.  Low utilization of funds during the first year of the Project, non-appointment of Malaria-Link Volunteers
(MLVs) and shortage of staff with the Core Project States have been cited as the main reasons for this position.
12.5     The Committee notes that to overcome these shortcomings, it has been decided that 100% expenditure for
payment to MLVs from the project funds be met during the Project period.   Additional staff has also  been provided to
the State Health/Malaria Control Societies for effective implementation of the Project.  The Committee hopes that these
measures will increase the utilization of funds by the States.  The Committee would like to be apprised about the
utilization of funds by the State Governments in the year 2002-2003 which is the last year of the EMCP.
12.6
          The Committee notes that spray coverage during the year 2000 was around 60% in the states of Arunachal
Pradesh, J & K, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tamil Nadu Tripura, U.P., West Bengal, A & N Islands, Chandigarh,
D & N Haveli, Daman & Diu and Delhi. 174.83 million population were targeted to be covered by residual insecticidal
spray in 2000-01, but only 67 million population could be covered as per reports received upto September, 2001.

has already been covered.   The revised strategy is also being implemented in Andhra Pradesh and Orissa with the
assistance of DFID and DANIDA at a cost of  Rs. 109.93 crores and Rs. 31.95 crores respectively to cover a total
population of 100 million.

anti-TB drugs to be supplied to various States/districts and non-procurement of binocular microscopes during the
financial year resulted in the reduction of funds meant for this purpose from Rs. 44.43 crores to Rs. 32.55 crores.

being funds meant to be released to the new 120 districts under the expansion plan could not be fully released due to
delayed approval of the EFC and CCEA.   Surplus funds lying with some district societies was another reason for
reduction.   The Committee observes that this trend has been there during the entire Ninth Plan period.   As per the
figures  available with the Committee, out of plan allocation of Rs. 581.00 crores from 1997-98 to 2001-02, the total
expenditure incurred  as  on 22.2.02 is only Rs. 398.48 crores.   The Committee finds that achievement level of Physical
Targets  under Sputum Examination and Sputum Positive Detection has also  been much  below the fixed targets  during
the Ninth Plan period.

some State Govts. for procurement of anti-TB drugs for sputum negative cases.   The Committee apprehends that

the State  Govt. for purchase of anti-TB drugs for sputum negative cases.  The Committee views this with serious

           The Committee notes that five different schemes for  involvement of NGOs have been envisaged and NGOs are

          The Programme was launched in 1976 as a 100%  Centrally sponsored Programme.   Its goal is to reduce the

IX        NATIONAL  MENTAL  HEALTH  PROGRAMME
19.1 The Programme, started in 1982, envisages a community based approach to the problem.   Funds are provided by
the Govt. to the State Govts. and the nodal institutes to  meet the expenditure on staff, equipments, training, IEC
activities etc.   At present, District Mental Health Programme is under implementation in 25 districts in 20 States.
19.2  Against a  Plan allocation of Rs. 4.00 crores in RE 2001-02, allocation in BE 2002-2003 has been astronomically
increased to Rs. 27.00 crores.  The Department  has informed that an increased allocation has been made for 2002-2003
based on the Tenth Five Year Plan proposal which envisages apart from sustaining the existing District Mental Health
Programme,   adding more districts to provide assistance for upgrading the infrastructure and modernization of the
existing mental health facilities in mental hospitals and psychiatric departments of medical colleges; to undertake
research in the field of mental health and to develop, disseminate and use   IEC programmes at national level.
19.3  The Committee notes that shortage of trained psychiatric manpower and lack of awareness regarding treatment are
the two main barriers to the provision of mental health services in the country.  The Committee has been given to
understand that about 4000 clinical psychologists,  psychiatric  social workers  and  psychiatric nurses are working in
the country which is inadequate to meet the total needs of  persons  with mental disorders in the country.  The shortage
of psychiatric manpower is felt in all the States, specially in rural areas.  The Committee strongly feels that there is a
need for having systematic evaluation regarding Statewise requirement of manpower.  The Committee also observes
that mental health programmes are being implemented in a varying degree by different States.   The Committee has
been informed that the District Mental Health Programme is to be enlarged and made more effective covering the  entire
country during the Tenth Plan.   The Committee feels that there  is an urgent need for expanding the mental health
services.  While  appreciating the substantive allocation of funds for this programme for 2002-03, the first year of Tenth
Plan, the Committee would like to emphasise that there should be regular and extensive monitoring at all levels to
ensure optimum and judicious utilization of funds.

 XX      PREVENTION  OF  FOOD  ADULTERATION  PROGRAMME
20.1  The subject of the Prevention of Food Adulteration is in the Concurrent list of the Constitution.  However, in
general, the enforcement of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is done by the State/UT. Governments.  The
Central Government primarily plays an advisory role in its implementation besides carrying out various statutory
functions/duties assigned to it under the various provisions of the Act.
20.2     Four Central Food Laboratories have been established under the Act, which work as appellate laboratories for
the purpose of analysis of samples of food lifted by the Food Inspectors of the States/U.Ts. and local bodies.  There are
82 Food Laboratories under the administrative control of various State/Union Territory Governments and Local Bodies.
20.3
             On being asked about experience of the Department in respect of administration of Prevention of Food
Adulteration Act and the Rules made thereunder, the Department has informed that some of the problems being faced
relate to inadequate enforcement at the level of the States.  There is a shortage of trained manpower, especially at the
level of food inspectors. Number of samples drawn for test and analysis has declined as also the cases in which
prosecutions have been launched or conviction obtained.  Capabilities of the State Food Laboratories are also required
to be augmented so that they can properly undertake analysis of contaminants.
20.4           The Department has also informed that the Government of India has been trying to assist the State Governments
by training of State Laboratory analysts and food inspectors and by supply of equipments to the laboratories.  The States
have been requested to increase their manpower for proper enforcement of the Act; to increase the budget to provide
proper facilities in the states laboratories and to utilize  the equipments provided by the Government of India properly;
to conduct investigational market surveys in a systematic way, with particular reference to items of mass consumption
and to keep a proper data bank of the results. 
20.5     From the feedback given by the Department, the Committee is left with no alternative but to believe that the
situation is indeed very grim so far as implementation of the   Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is concerned.   It
seems that with the load of so many Disease Control Programmes, this aspect of health management is  not getting the
due impetus from any State in the country.   The Committee is therefore, of the view that drastic measures are required
to be taken.   The Committee recommends that an overall review of Prevention of Food Adulteration Programme with
special focus on status of State laboratories, requirement of more labs and necessary staff therefor should be initiated
without any further delay.

have constituted State  Health Malaria Control Societies.   Remaining States are yet to follow suit.   The Committee
enjoins upon the Department to vigorously  pursue with the defaulter States.  (Para 12.9)
XIII      KALA-AZAR CONTROL  PROGRAMME
The Committee  hopes that with the beginning of the  Tenth Plan, things will improve in Bihar.   The
Committee, however, is of the  opinion that mere provision of enhanced Central assistance will not be  sufficient.   What
is required is intensive  monitoring in co-ordination with the State Govts. of Bihar and W. Bengal.  (Para 13.2)
XIV.   JAPANESE ENCEPHALITIS (JE)
            The Committee finds it rather surprising that there is no separate budget provision available for JE prevention  
and control.   The Committee strongly feels that States tackling these problems out of their  resources  does not  make
any sense due to their generally poor   financial position.   The Department must be fully aware about lack of motivation
on the part of most of the States in implementation of health Programmes in spite of central funding.  Diversion of need-
based support for  outbreak containment out of resources available under NAMP  cannot be considered a sound
strategy.   What is required is a well-planned programme with separate funding for control of JE. (Para 14.3)
XV.      NATIONAL  T.B. CONTROL  PROGRAMME
The Committee finds that achievement level of Physical Targets  under Sputum Examination and Sputum
Positive Detection has also  been much  below the fixed targets  during the Ninth Plan period. (Para 15.2)
The Committee recommends that the Department should pursue the submission of Utilisation Certificates with
all concerned State Govts. (Para 15.3)
The Committee would like to emphasise  that participation of Public Representatives in formal functions will not
achieve the desired results.   What is required is an exercise to obtain the feedback from the local Public Representatives
regarding the various ongoing activities  of the Programme in their areas.   Besides that, there is a need for having
random surveys/surprise inspections by Central teams.  Last year the Committee had desired that the Department should
take action for evolving a more effective monitoring mechanism.   The Committee strongly feels that mere taking note
of the advice regarding random surveys/surprise inspections does not serve any purpose.  The Department has to take
initiative  in this direction without any delay. (Para 15.5) 
The Committee strongly feels that in a country like India which accounts for nearly 1/3
rd of the global TB
burden, where every year there are approximately 22 lakhs new TB cases, and where one  person dies from TB every
minute and more than 5 lakhs every year, all the inherent  flaws in the Programme at all levels need to be eliminated at
the earliest. (Para 15.6)
XVI.    NATIONAL  LEPROSY  ERADICATION  PROGRAMME
The Committee notes that there has been optimum utilization of funds under the Programme during Ninth Plan.  
Against total allocation of Rs.388.00 crores, reported expenditure figures are Rs. 384.26 crores.  Similarly,  achievement
level of Physical Targets as per the parameters of Case Detection, Case Treatment and Case Discharge have been many
times more. (Para 16.3)
The Committee observes that there is no dearth of funds under the Programme and a large number of NGOs are
also involved with quite a few reported to be doing good work.  Special focus under 2
nd Phase of World Bank Assisted
Project is also there on the eight high endemic States.   The Committee, however, feels that Bihar being  the most
affected State,  there is a special need for extensive monitoring of   implementation of all the components of the Project
in Bihar.   The Committee is of the view that all efforts should be made to provide training in leprosy services to all
General Health Services Staff, specially in the most affected districts  of the State.   Campaigns for enhancing public
awareness about the disease would also contribute a lot. (Para 16.4)

XVII    NATIONAL  PROGRAMME  FOR  CONTROL  OF  BLINDNESS
The Committee recommends that all these proposals should be activated  at the earliest so that remote and tribal
areas do not remain deprived of the benefits of National Programme for Control of Blindness.  (Para 17.2)
The Committee strongly recommends that the Department should closely monitor the implementation of
different components of the National Programme for Control of Blindness in States where achievement level continues
to be very low.   Every effort should be made to ascertain the inherent constraints being faced by  the implementing
agencies.  (Para 17.5)
The Committee would like to be apprised about the findings of the Survey regarding prevalence and causes of
blindness and impact of the Blindness Control Project in these districts. (Para 17.6)
XVIII        NATIONAL  AIDS  CONTROL  PROGRAMME
            The Committee would like to be apprised of the findings of the sample survey. (Para 18.3)
            The Committee notes the efforts made by the Department in expanding the base of NGOs and recommends that
the Department should take up this  issue with other States where NGO activity is not there. (Para 18.4)
The Committee notes that the importance of Reproductive tract infection (RTI) including sexually transmitted
diseases (STD) has increased with the introduction of HIV/AIDS epidemic in the country.  (Para 18.5) 
The Committee is constrained to note that there is a very wide gap between target population covered and
population actually attended the camps. The Committee feels that this low achievement level is a clear indication that
there was a lack of awareness amongst people about the Family Health Awareness campaign.  The Committee,
therefore, recommends that a very extensive publicity  drive should precede the launching of such Family Health
Awareness Campaigns.  Only then maximum coverage would be there.  (Para 18.6)
            The Committee is of the view that there is apparent contradiction between the two clarifications given by the
Department.   As per  the ATN, the World Bank administration has agreed to reduce the requirement for production
capability from 25% to 10% of the tendered quantity.  As per the second clarification, World Bank has raised the past
supply criteria to 50% from 25%.  In the earlier reply, country has been divided into four regions.   However,  second
clarification mentions eight regions.  The Committee would like to be enlightened in this regard. (Para 18.9)
IX        NATIONAL  MENTAL  HEALTH  PROGRAMME
The Committee notes that shortage of trained psychiatric manpower and lack of awareness regarding treatment are
the two main barriers to the provision of mental health services in the country.  The Committee has been given to
understand that about 4000 clinical psychologists,  psychiatric  social workers  and  psychiatric nurses are working in
the country which is inadequate to meet the total needs of  persons  with mental disorders in the country.  The shortage
of psychiatric manpower is felt in all the States, specially in rural areas.  The Committee strongly feels that there is a
need for having systematic evaluation regarding Statewise requirement of manpower.  The Committee also observes
that mental health programmes are being implemented in a varying degree by different States.   The Committee has
been informed that the District Mental Health Programme is to be enlarged and made more effective covering the  entire
country during the Tenth Plan.   The Committee feels that there  is an urgent need for expanding the mental health
services.  While  appreciating the substantive allocation of funds for this programme for 2002-03, the first year of Tenth
Plan, the Committee would like to emphasise that there should be regular and extensive monitoring at all levels to
ensure optimum and judicious utilization of funds.       (Para 19.3)
 XX      PREVENTION  OF  FOOD  ADULTERATION  PROGRAMME
From the feedback given by the Department, the Committee is left with no alternative but to believe that the
situation is indeed very grim so far as implementation of the   Prevention of Food Adulteration Act is concerned.   It
seems that with the load of so many Disease Control Programmes, this aspect of health management is  not getting the
due impetus from any State in the country.   The Committee is therefore, of the view that drastic measures are required
to be taken.   The Committee recommends that an overall review of Prevention of Food Adulteration Programme with
special focus on status of State laboratories, requirement of more labs and necessary staff therefor should be initiated
without any further delay.  (Para 20.5)
XXI        DEVELOPMENT OF NURSING SERVICE

               The Committee feels that in a situation when large number of the people of this country particularly living in
remote and far flung areas are outside the reach of Health Care Delivery System, continuing with such a process which
makes the opening  of new Nursing Schools a long drawn one is not desirable.  The Committee, therefore, recommends
that appropriate steps should be taken so that avoidable procedural requirements are done away with.  The Committee
would also like to be apprised about the full details regarding Projects of Nursing Schools/colleges sanctioned and lying
pending (Statewise). (Para 21.2)
XXII    DRUGS  STANDARD CONTROL  PROGRAMME
               The Committee feels that the silence on the part of State Governments in furnishing the requite information is
perhaps due to their inability to  fill up the vacant posts.  The Committee views this very seriously and recommends that
the Department should pursue this matter relentlessly  with the State Governments. The Committee notes that there are
no drug testing laboratories in Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Pondicherry, Andaman & Nicobar
Islands, Chandidgarh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Uttaranchal, Jharkhand and Chattisgarh.  Drug testing labs in States in
general except for the labs in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh fall below the required
levels.  The Committee finds that a countrywide auditing of all drug testing laboratories including Govt. testing
laboratories has been initiated.   The Committee welcomes this initiative  and hopes that this will result in proper
assessment of requirements in this vital sector and resultant follow-up action. (Para 22.3)
XXIII      HOSPITAL WASTE MANAGEMENT
On the perusal of the list, the Committee is shocked to find that  in respect of the States/UT  of Bihar, Manipur, 
Rajasthan and Chandigarh no action has been initiated by the State Pollution Control Boards or Pollution Control
Committees against the erring hospitals/nursing homes.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that this matter should
be taken up with the concerned Ministry, without any delay.  (Para 23.3)
XXIV   IMPLEMENTATION OF HEALTH PROGRAMMES IN  NORTH EAST SECTOR
Status of various National Health Programme in North-Eastern States is as follows :
NATIONAL PROGRAMME FOR CONTROL OF BLINDNESS:-
         The Committee observes  that Cataract Surgery performance rate  is low in all States except Tripura.   Assam is
one of the lowest performing States in the country with Cataract Surgery rate as low as 162 operations per lakh
population against the national rate of 400. (Para 24.2)
         The Committee notes that State Blindness Control Societies have been constituted so far in the States of
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura only.   The Committee has been given to understand that eye care
infrastructure is weak in  NE region, particularly  in Assam.   Very few NGOs are located in the region.   Number of
Eye surgeons is also very inadequate.   The Committee feels that in spite of adequate funds  being provided, the
programme is not functioning well.   Non-setting up/non-functioning of District Blindness Control Societies and lack of
NGO involvement seem to be the two major handicaps.   The Committee recommends that the  Department should
vigorously  pursue  the implementation of the Programme with all the NE States. (Para 24.3)
The Committee apprehends that reason for the drastic cut in allocation of funds may be unspent balances lying
with the State Govts.   If that be so, it is  a cause of serious concern.   The Committee would like to be enlightened on
this aspect. (Para 24.8)
NATIONAL AIDS CONTROL PROGRAMME 
The Committee is shocked to find that not a single North-Eastern State has been able to fully utilize the funds
allocated to them and the States of Assam and Tripura failed to utilize even a single penny.  The Committee feels that
there is something seriously amiss in respect of these States and recommends that the Department should make an
enquiry into the matter.  (Para 24.10)

PREFACE
 
            I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this
Hundred-Seventeenth Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand No.44) of the Department of
Family Welfare,  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for the year 2002-2003.
 
2.         The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from the Department of Family
Welfare and also heard the Secretary and other Officials of that Department   on the said Demands for Grants in its
meeting held on 28
th   March, 2002.
 
3.         The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meeting held on     24th  April, 2002.
 
 
NEW DELHI
April  24, 2002
Vaishakha 4,   1924 (Saka)
ARJUN SINGH
Chairman

         Standing Committee on
Human Resource Development
 
REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
1.1       The Census of 2001 had indicated the population of India as 1027 million with 531 million males and 496
million females.    In the decade  1991-2001, nearly 181 million persons were added to the population of India.  
Population increased at an annual exponential growth rate of 1.93 percent in the decade.  As per the latest Sample
Registration System (SRS) estimates, the annual growth rate of population is 1.74% (1999).  
1.2       The eight States of U.P., Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Uttaranchal, Chhatisgarh and Orissa,
which currently constitute nearly 44% of the total population of India, are projected to comprise 48% of the total
population in 2016.   In other words, these States alone will contribute an anticipated 55% increase during the period
1996-2016.    Demographic outcome in these States will determine the timing and size of population at which India
achieves population stabilisation.
1.3       The three most significant factors that can curtail the growth of population are increase in the use of
contraceptives, improvement in the mother’s health and survival of children.  All the programmes of the Department of
Family Welfare are accordingly planned and being implemented for pursuing a combination of these three issues.
1.4       During the Tenth  Plan the main approach of family welfare programme will be:
(i)
                  To assess the needs for Reproductive and Child Health (RCH);
(ii)                To provide need based ,client centered and demand driven RCH care;
(iii)               To strengthen the infrastructure for service delivery and bridging the gap in essential infrastructure and
manpower;
(iv)              Providing additional assistance to poorly performing districts and ensuring uninterrupted supply of drugs
and equipments;  and

woman and BCG, Measles, DPT and Polio for infants have increased in comparison to the preceding year.
1.6       In respect of achievement of performance in Family Planning methods and to achieve the long term goals, the
following levels of contraceptives were achieved during 1996-97 to 2000-2001.

that in the case of sterilisation, the number of male sterilisation is much below the desired level and recommends that
the Department should take appropriate steps so that the participation of males is increased in Family Planning
methods.  
1.7       The Committee understands that under the Community Needs Assessment Approach (CNAA), an action plan is
prepared each year at the district level based  on the need assessment done by ANMs of Sub-Centre at village level.  In
the beginning of the financial year, the health worker will first complete the house-to-house survey.  Based on this
survey, Eligible Couple Register is updated by the ANM.  The Committee has been informed that the State Govts. are 
impressed from time to time to ensure that the Sub-Centre action is got prepared for each Sub-Centre in the State.  The
Committee has its own doubts about the implementation of this annual exercise, which is most essential for successful
implementation of Family Welfare Programme, specially in the remote and inaccessible areas.  The Committee strongly
feels that surprise inspections in the performing as well as non-performing districts by Central teams/dedicated
NGOs/Social Workers can bring out the ground reality.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should initiate such an exercise in 2002-2003.

II          BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
2.1              The Committee has been informed that allocation for the Department for  2002-2003 is Rs. 4953.83 crores
against Rs. 4232.38 crores in BE 2001-2002 which was  reduced to Rs. 3721.67 crores at RE stage.   This represents  an
increase of Rs. 721.55 crores over the previous year.
2.2
              Commenting on the allocation, the Department submitted that the Annual Plan proposal for the year 2002-2003
was Rs. 7590.56 crores.  However, an allocation of Rs 4953.83 crores was approved by the Planning Commission.  As a
result of cut in plan proposal, funding of the infrastructural units in the States will be the most affected.   Besides that, 
other schemes like contractual appointments under RCH Programme, adolescent health care, supply of Dai kits,
promoting institutional deliveries, civil works at Sub Centres, urban slum project and strengthening of primary health
care infrastructure, may also be curtailed.
2.3
              The Committee  has also been given to understand that during 2001-2002, a cut of 710.00 crores (plan) was
proposed by the Ministry of Finance on the basis of expenditure  incurred by the Department till October, 2001
(51.19%).   However,  subsequently an assurance was given by the Ministry of Finance that if 75% expenditure was
incurred by the Department by December, 2001, the cut made in the outlay will be restored.    However, despite meeting
the targetted expenditure and the representations made at the highest level, the cut of Rs. 710 crores was only reduced to
Rs. 510 crores.  
2.4              The Committee agrees in principle with the Department's contention of there being no case for resorting to a cut
of Rs. 700.00 crores at the RE stage in 2001-2002 by the Ministry of Finance.  The Committee also notes that total plan
allocation of Rs. 3700.00 crores in 2001-2002 is anticipated to be utilised. Actual expenditure figures are not available
at present.  The Committee, however observes that during 2000-2001, against a higher projected requirement, plan
allocation was Rs. 3500.00 crores which was reduced to Rs. 3200.00 crores at the RE stage.  Actual expenditure was
even less i.e. Rs. 3071.35 crores.  The Committee strongly feels that inview of much higher allocation of Rs. 4930.00
crores in 2002-2003, the Department should ensure that funds allocated under various schemes are utilised optimally
and strictly as per the action plan to strengthen its case of higher allocation.
III        RURAL FAMILY WELFARE SERVICES
3.1
              The Rural Family Welfare Centres were set up at all block level PHCs sanctioned upto 1.4.1980 to provide
Family Planning and MCH Services in rural areas.  There are 5435 such centres functioning in the Country.  Besides
that, to provide basic health and family welfare services to the rural population 1,37,311 Sub-Centres  are currently
functioning out of which 97,757 Sub-Centres were funded by the Department till now. 
3.2              The Committee was informed that a Consultative Committee consisting of the representatives of the Planning
Commission, Department of Expenditure, States of Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan was constituted by
the Department in 1998.   The Committee examined the SWAP proposal between Rural Family Welfare Centres and
Sub-Centres and strongly recommended that in view of the importance of the rural Sub-Centres for the Family Welfare
Programme, and as the Rural Family Welfare Centres have lost their original identity and have become part of primary
health centre complexes at the block level, the Department of Family Welfare should assume the responsibility of
funding all 1,37,311 existing Sub-Centres.   In exchange, for accepting this responsibility the States should take over the
financial liability of maintaining the Rural Family Welfare Centres  (RFWC) numbering 5435.
3.3       The Department  also informed that the main purpose of the SWAP is to streamline the system of financing the
Sub-Centres. As the Sub-Centres were established by Central Government and State Governments during different time
periods it is difficult to assess the impact of the programme run by the Department.   Therefore, there was a need to
bring all the Sub-Centres under one umbrella for effective monitoring of the programme.   The Planning Commission
insisted  that a consensus be developed among the States on the issue of swaping these responsibilities between the State
and Department of Family Welfare.     The Committee in its 101
st Report had also recommended that the issue needed
to be discussed with the States/UTs before any decision was taken in this regard.  The Committee, however, notes that a
decision has already been taken to implement the SWAP proposal from 1.4.2002.  Therefore there  is no proposal for
requirement of Funds for RFWCs in the Tenth Plan.  Accordingly, no allocation has been made in BE 2002-2003.
3.4       The Committee is surprised to note that a final decision has already been taken by the Department inspite of
there being no consensus on this issue among the States.  According to the Department itself, outcome of
implementation of SWAP proposal will be that some states will be in an advantageous position by saving the funds and

5.1       Reproductive and Child Health Programme is the flagship programme of Family Welfare, which combines
trinity of objectives viz. reproductive health, Child survival and fertility regulation. The Programme is primarily offered
through Primary Health Infrastructure.  The overall goals of the programme are to reduce maternal and infant mortality
and morbidity and unwanted fertility and contribute thereto stabilization of population.

Department  should club  all the immunization related activities under one head.   Acting on the advice of the Planning
Commission, the allocation for polio activities and vaccines for routine immunization related activities which stands at
Rs. 376 crores and Rs. 141 crores respectively have been separated from the RCH Programme which in-turn resulted in
decreased allocation  for RCH Programme in BE 2002-2003.

Programme and feels that the Departmentshould, in the same vein carry similar rationalization/ restructuring,  
wherever possible, in respect of other programmes.

VII       POST PARTUM PROGRAMME
Post Partum Programme is a maternity centered hospital based approach to Family Welfare Programme covering
550 Post Partum Centres at district level and 1012 Post Partum Centres at sub-district level hospitals.   The objective of
the programme is to provide antenatal,  natal and post-natal services to expectant mothers and also to provide Family
Planning Services, besides diagnosing early cases of cervical cancer.   An allocation of  Rs 135.00 crores was made for
Post Partum Programme in BE 2001-2002.   However, no allocation has been made for the year 2002-2003.   Giving
reasons, the Department has replied that the Planning Commission has decided to transfer the Post Partum Programme
to the States/UTs w.e.f. 1.4.2002.  The Committee would be interested to know as to the precise reasons that weighed in
favour of transfer of this Programme to the States/UTs.
VIII      DISTRIBUTION OF CONTRACEPTIVES
8.1
              Allocation of Rs. 117.00 crores made under the head Free Distribution of Conventional Contraceptive in BE
2001-2002 has been increased to Rs. 181.80 crores in 2002-2003.  Explaining the reasons for increase,  the Department
has informed that due to increasing number of younger couples, the demand for condoms under free distribution from

proposed.
8.2       The Department has further informed that as regards allocation of additional quantities of conventional
contraceptives in the States, these would be allocated proportionately in relation  to utilisation and demand of the
respective States.   The unmet need in condom under free supply scheme is nearly 30% whereas in Oral Contraceptive
Pill (OCP) it is around 10%.   Attempts will be made to fill up these gaps.   The additional allocation would be required
for the purchase of the raw material for OCP which is no more available under external assistance and the same has to
be met from domestic resources.
8.3       In regard to the quality of Nirodh, the Committee has been given to understand that  19% users have rated it
under free supply scheme as okay,  75% as good and 6% have rated as very good.    The Committee feels that the
quality of condoms goes a long way in its acceptance by the users.    The Committee is also of the view that poor quality
may lead to unwanted pregnancy and reproductive tract infections.    The Committee,  therefore, recommends that the
Department should ensure that only the best quality of latex is used in manufacturing of condoms.

XI       NEW INITIATIVES
11.1    An allocation of Rs.34.24 crores was made in BE 2001-02 for new initiatives which has been substantially
increased to Rs. 170.80 crores in BE 2002-2003.  The Department has informed the Committee that the enhanced
provision is proposed to be utilized for undertaking new initiatives like Community Incentive Scheme, Family Welfare
linked Health Insurance Scheme, Convergence of Services, Empowered Action Group, Other Initiatives, Strengthening
MIs through CNAA, Implementation of PNDT Act etc. as envisaged in the National Population Policy 2000.
11.2    The Committee feels that the problem of exponential growth of population is the mother of all the problems of
this country. No matter howsoever, high is the growth rate of national economy it will be insufficient to meet the
economic needs of the people if the rate of population growth  is not arrested.  The Committee is of the considered
view that unless the factors which are contributory to the uncontrolled growth of population, such as illiteracy
particularly in woman, poverty etc. are appropriately addressed, we will have no escape from this unfortunate
situation.   All the political parties/groups owe their duty to the country to sit together and evolve a consensus in this
regard.
OBSERVBATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE
I           INTRODUCTION
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the percentage of coverage in 2000-2001 in respect of TT for
pregnant woman and BCG, Measles, DPT and Polio for infants have increased in comparison to the preceding year.
(Para 1.5)
The Committee notes that though there is a marginal increase in the case of sterilisation and C.C. users, the
number of IUD Insertions and O.P. users has decreased in the year 2000-2001 in comparison to 1999-2000.    The
Committee feels that in the case of sterilisation, the number of male sterilisation is much below the desired level and
recommends that the Department should take appropriate steps so that the participation of males is increased in Family
Planning methods.   (Para 1.6)
            The Committee understands that under the Community Needs Assessment Approach (CNAA), an action plan is
prepared each year at the district level based  on the need assessment done by ANMs of Sub-Centre at village level.  In
the beginning of the financial year, the health worker will first complete the house-to-house survey.  Based on this
survey, Eligible Couple Register is updated by the ANM.  The Committee has been informed that the State Govts. are 
impressed from time to time to ensure that the Sub-Centre action is got prepared for each Sub-Centre in the State.  The
Committee has its own doubts about the implementation of this annual exercise, which is most essential for successful
implementation of Family Welfare Programme, specially in the remote and inaccessible areas.  The Committee strongly
feels that surprise inspections in the performing as well as non-performing districts by Central teams/dedicated
NGOs/Social Workers can bring out the ground reality.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department
should initiate such an exercise in 2002-2003. (Para 1.7)
II          BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
The Committee agrees in principle with the Department's contention of there being no case for resorting to a cut
of Rs. 700.00 crores at the RE stage in 2001-2002 by the Ministry of Finance.  The Committee also notes that total plan
allocation of Rs. 3700.00 crores in 2001-2002 is anticipated to be utilised. Actual expenditure figures are not available
at present.  The Committee, however observes that during 2000-2001, against a higher projected requirement, plan
allocation was Rs. 3500.00 crores which was reduced to Rs. 3200.00 crores at the RE stage.  Actual expenditure was
even less i.e. Rs. 3071.35 crores.  The Committee strongly feels that inview of much higher allocation of Rs. 4930.00
crores in 2002-2003, the Department should ensure that funds allocated under various schemes are utilised optimally

and strictly as per the action plan to strengthen its case of higher allocation. (Para 2.4)
III        RURAL FAMILY WELFARE SERVICES
            The Committee is surprised to note that a final decision has already been taken by the Department inspite of
there being no consensus on this issue among the States.  According to the Department itself, outcome of
implementation of SWAP proposal will be that some states will be in an advantageous position by saving the funds and
some States in a disadvantageous position.  For example, as per the information made available to the Committee,
whereas additionalliability in the case of Chandigarh will be only Rs. 7 lakhs, for West Bengal it will be as high as Rs.
17.74 crores.  The Committee wonders about the fate of Rural Family Welfare Centres in view of no allocation being
made by the Department in BE 2002-2003.  The Committee would, therefore, like to emphasise that the issue of
compensating the affected states should be sorted out at the earliest.  (Para 3.4)
The Committee is sympathetic to  grievance of some of the State Governments  who will be placed
disadvantageously as a result of the proposal.  The Committee recommends that the Department should vigorously
pursue its proposal with the Planning Commission for compensating the affected states.   The Department should make
concerted efforts to fix a rational basis for distribution of liabilities amongst the State Governments so that no injustice
is done to any State.  (Para 3.5)
Given the tight financial position of the State Governments, the Committee feels that it is a great challenge for
them. (Para 3.6) 
The Committee is constrained to note that the major defaulting States in respect of setting up of Sub-Centres are
Bihar, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Orissa, Meghalaya, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi. In
respect of PHCs these are Assam, A.P., Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Nagaland,
Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Delhi.  As far as CHCs are concerned, Assam, A.P., Bihar, Haryana,
MadhyaPradesh, Maharashtra, Meghalaya, Orissa, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal
and Delhi are the major defaulters. (Para 3.10)
The Committee is perturbed  to note that targets for setting up of Sub-Centres, PHCs and CHCs during Ninth
Plan seem to have been prescribed for namesake only.  The achievement level for the first four years of Ninth Plan
1997-2001 clearly indicates this assessment-
 Targets Achievement level (upto 2000-2001)
Sub-Centres 7686 1053
PHCs 1521 693
CHCs 2903 410
(Para 3.11)
The Committee recommends that the Department should take necessary steps to achieve the  target of setting up
of Sub-centres, PHCs and CHCs.  The Committee also fails  to understand as to how such a large number of states have
failed to achieve the target of setting up of Sub-centres, PHCs and CHCs and therefore recommends that the Department
should try to find out the reasons behind this phenomenon.  (Para 3.12)
The Committee also observes that in many States, the number of established Sub-Centres exceeds the projected
requirements as per 2002 projected population.  Financial liability with regard to all existing 1,37,311 Sub-Centres is to
be borne by the Central Govt. from 2002-2003.  The justification of bearing the expenditure in respect of excess Sub-
Centres set up in different States by the Centre needs to be explored from all aspects.  Specially in view of the fact that
proposal of the Department for financing the establishment of new Sub-Centres under the 100% Centrally Sponsored
Scheme is pending with the Ministry of Finance and shortage of Sub-Centres is there in large number of States. (Para
3.13)
The Committee laments at the lackadaisical approach of the Department in getting the data collected from
various States and desires that these may be obtained and  furnished to the Committee at the earliest .  (Para 3.15)
The Committee feels that  ANMs and LHVs are the persons responsible for delivering Family Welfare Services
to rural people and therefore recommends that the Department should make concerted efforts to get  the posts of ANMs
and LHVs  filled up at the earliest in respect of the weak performing states.  (Para 3.16)
IV        URBAN FAMILY WELFARE SERVICES

The Committee is of the view  that for improving outreach service delivery system in urban slums,
reorganisation of Urban Family Welfare Centres should be made at the earliest.    Therefore, the Committee
recommends that the Department should make adequate provision for reorganisation of Urban Family Welfare Centres
in 2002-2003. (Para 4.4)
V         REPRODUCTIVE AND CHILD HEALTH PROGRAMME (RCH)
The Committee notes with appreciation the rationalization done by the Department in restructuring the RCH
Programme and feels that the Department should, in the same vein carry similar rationalization/ restructuring,  
wherever possible, in respect of other programmes.     (Para 5.3)
The Committee feels that the underutilization of funds  by the State governments is quite alarming  as it reflects
that the Programme is not being implemented properly at the ground level. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
the Department should take up the matter with the concerned  States and try to find out the reasons behind under
utilization of funds by them and take necessary remedial measures. (Para 5.4)
The Committee expresses its dissatisfaction that the Department has not so far taken up the matter with the State
Govts even after almost a year has passed.   It desires that this may be done at the earliest and the outcome may be
intimated to it. (Para 5.5)
            Noting the efforts made by the Department, the Committee feels that though some progress has been made in
respect of Infant mortality rate, percentage of safe delivery etc.,   they are still very high in comparison to even a
number  of developing countries.   Some States like Assam, Bihar, M.P., U.P., Orissa and Rajasthan continue to perform
much below the National Average.   In view of this, the Committee recommends  that the Department should make
extra efforts to improve the performance in these states. (Para 5.8)
The Committee feels that the Department should approach the concerned States for bringing out the necessary
improvements/modifications in the schemes for a better implementation of the same. (Para 5.9)
The Committee recommends that the Department should pursue with the remaining States also.  Efforts should
also be made to extend this scheme to more districts. (Para 5.10)
VI        STRENGTHENING OF IMMUNISATION PROGRAMME AND ERADICATION OF POLIO
            The Committee is deeply anguished to find that a cut in the allocation at the RE stage was made due to delay in
procurement of equipment and stores.    The Committee feels that such delays seriously affect the implementation of
Family WelfareProgrammes.  It,  therefore, recommends that the  Department should inquire into as to whether this
delay could have been avoided and if so, the responsibility should be fixed in this regard.  It should also take extra
precaution so that such delays are avoided in future.  (Para 6.2)
In case of BCG vaccination and DPT Immunization the Committee is happy to note that the all India
achievement is more than 100%.  However, again Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland are the low-performing
States.   The same can be said about DPT Immunisation coverage.    (Para 6.3)
             The Committee observes that the States like Bihar, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya  and Nagaland continue to
perform much  below the national average over the years in all the immunization programmes.  Another disturbing
feature noticed by the Committee  is the downward trend in the percentage of coverage during the last three years of
Ninth Plan in respect of some States.  The Committee therefore, recommends that the Department should identify such
States as are performing below the national average and take special steps to strengthen the immunization scheme in
such States.  (Para 6.4)
VII       POST PARTUM PROGRAMME
The Committee would be interested to know as to the precise reasons that weighed in favour of transfer of this
Programme to the States/UTs.
VIII      DISTRIBUTION OF CONTRACEPTIVES
            In regard to the quality of Nirodh, the Committee has been given to understand that  19% users have rated it
under free supply scheme as okay,  75% as good and 6% have rated as very good.    The Committee feels that the
quality of condoms goes a long way in its acceptance by the users.    The Committee is also of the view that poor quality

may lead to unwanted pregnancy and reproductive tract infections.    The Committee,  therefore, recommends that the
Department should ensure that only the best quality of latex is used in manufacturing of condoms.  (Para 8.3)
IX        AREA PROJECTS
            The Committee is perturbed to note the reasons behind cut in RE 2001-2002.  The  Committee feels that reasons
like slow implementation of a Project and delay in finalization of cost bifurcation etc. reflect  administrative
inexpediency and therefore recommends that the Department should take necessary steps to avoid such procedural
delays in future.  It also gives an impression that the Project is not being effectively implemented. (Para 9.3)
X         INFORMATION EDUCATION AND COMMUNICATION
            The Committee notes with appreciation the steps taken by the Department in involving local people for IEC
activities.   The Committee, however, feels that such decentralisation of fund allocation sometimes result in
misuse/misappropriation  of funds and therefore recommends that the Department should keep a strict vigil on the
utilisation of funds by the district and local authorities. (Para 10.4)
XI       NEW INITIATIVES
           The Committee feels that the problem of exponential growth of population is the mother of all the problems of
this country. No matter howsoever, high is the growth rate of national economy it will be insufficient to meet the
economic needs of the people if the rate of population growth  is not arrested.  The Committee is of the considered
view that unless the factors which are contributory to the uncontrolled growth of population, such as illiteracy
particularly in woman, poverty etc. are appropriately addressed, we will have no escape from this unfortunate
situation.   All the political parties/groups owe their duty to the country to sit together and evolve a consensus in this
regard.  (Para 11.2)

PREFACE
 
            I,  the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource
Development, having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this 
Hundred – Eighteenth  Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand No.43) of the Department of
Indian Systems of Medicine & Homoeopathy,  Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for the year 2002-2003.
2.         The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from the Department of Indian
Systems of Medicine & Homoeopathy, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and also heard the Secretary and other
Officials of that Department  on the said Demands for Grants in its meeting held on 3
rd   April, 2002.
3.         The Committee considered the Draft Report and adopted the same in its meeting held on 22nd   April, 2002.
 
NEW DELHI
April  22, 2002
Vaisakha 2, 1924 (Saka)
ARJUN SINGH
Chairman,
Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on
                         Human Resource Development
 
 
REPORT
I           INTRODUCTION
The Department of Indian Systems of Medicine and Homoeopathy was set up by the Government of India as an
independent Department in March, 1995 under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.  The main objective of the
Department is to provide focused attention for the proper development and  propagation of ISM&H, namely Ayurveda,
Siddha, Unani, Homoeopathy, Yoga and Naturopathy and to fully utilise the potentials of these systems.
II          PERFORMANCE  DURING  NINTH FIVE  YEAR  PLAN
2.1       The thrust areas identified for intervention during the Ninth Plan period were as indicated below:-
Effective use of ISM&H systems for health for all and for better patient care system.
-
                      Upgradation of medical educational facilities and improvement in standards of ISM&H medical education.
-                      Focus on research and development efforts
-                      Increasing availability of raw material
-                      Setting up of National Institute for each system.
-                      Development/Strengthening of pharmacopoeial  laboratories and Strengthening of State Government
pharmacies
2.2       Keeping in view the thrust areas, the following schemes were prepared by the Department  for implementation
during the  plan period:-
-
                      Scheme for strengthening of Pharmacopoeia Committee on ISM
-                      Scheme of grant-in-aid for  development of ISM&H UG colleges
-                      Scheme of grant-in-aid for Re-orientation for in-service training programme

118th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/118threport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:26]
-                      Scheme of assistance to PG medical education in ISM&H
-                      Scheme of assistance to State Drug Testing Laboratories/Pharmacies
-                      Scheme of assistance for Extra-Mural Research Project through Research Institutions
-                      Setting up of Medicinal Plants Board
-                      Innovative Schemes for development of medicinal plants,
-                      Scheme on Information, Education and Communication
-                      Scheme of assistance for International Exchange Programme/Seminars/Workshops on ISM&H.
 
2.3              The plan allocation and utilization of funds during the Ninth Plan period (year wise)is indicated below:
                                      (Rs. in crores)
Year BE RE Actual Expenditure
1997-98 32.30 32.80 33.04
1998-99 50.00 50.00 50.02
1999-2000 59.13 55.00 49.04
2000-2001 100.00 90.00 79.45
2001-2002 120.00 90.00 51.49 (upto Feb.2002)
 
2.4       From the above table, the Committee infers that  the  Department has fully utilised the allocated funds during the
first two  years of the Plan. Thereafter, the trend of BE allocation being reduced at RE stage and that too remaining
under-utilised started. The Committee was given to understand that tremendous increase in the Plan allocation for 2000-
01 as compared to previous year's allocation, put a strain on its absorption capacity. The Committee observes that
instead of there being any improvement in 2001-02, the last year of Ninth Plan, situation has worsened. The Committee
strongly feels that although the Department succeeded in getting enhanced allocation by projecting higher requirements
meant for expansion of ongoing Schemes and launching of many new Schemes, the Department failed to achieve both
the physical and financial targets during 2000-01 and 2001-02. The Committee notes that a large number of new
schemes were proposed to be launched during Ninth Plan period. However, so far as their implementation is concerned,
performance has been dismal.   In the last year of the Ninth Plan, i.e.2001-02, as many as eleven new schemes were
there, out of which some were yet to be finalised due to procedural bottlenecks and in the case of others, due to late
approval, schemes were yet to take off.
2.5       The Committee observes that as many as nineteen new schemes have been identified by the Department for
initiation during the Tenth Plan period. Scheme of CGHS Expansion in dispensaries is one of such Schemes. The
Committee is, however constrained to note that this Scheme was proposed to be launched during the Ninth Plan.  
However, for reasons unknown to the Committee, the Scheme was dropped during 1999-2000.  The Committee is
surprised to note that this Scheme is again included in the list of new schemes  to be launched during Tenth Plan.   In
contrast, fate of Schemes like 'Health for all through preventive and promotive Programme of ISMH', 'Speciality clinics
on ISMH',  ‘Indian Homoeopathy Pharmacy Council' and 'ISM Pharmacy Council’ is not known. The Committee hopes
that proper planning and preparatory exercise with regard to finalization and approval in respect of all these proposed
new schemes must have been done before making budget provision for the same in 2002-03. The Committee would like
to be enlightened in this regard.

Perhaps, the decision about recognition of other ayurvedic institutions/centers for CGHS beneficiaries lies with the

Central Council of Indian Medicine.   The Committee observes that the Central Register pertaining to only six states i.e.
Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Haryana and Tamil Nadu out of the eighteen states where practitioners of
ISM are registered has been prepared so far and that too for varying period of time.    The Committee urges upon the
Department to expedite the preparation of the Central register of Indian Medicare in respect of all the concerned States.
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE
II          PERFORMANCE  DURING  NINTH FIVE  YEAR  PLAN
            From the above table, the Committee infers that  the  Department has fully utilised the allocated funds during the
first two  years of the Plan. Thereafter, the trend of BE allocation being reduced at RE stage and that too remaining
under-utilised started. The Committee was given to understand that tremendous increase in the Plan allocation for 2000-
01 as compared to previous year's allocation, put a strain on its absorption capacity. The Committee observes that
instead of there being any improvement in 2001-02, the last year of Ninth Plan, situation has worsened. The Committee
strongly feels that although the Department succeeded in getting enhanced allocation by projecting higher requirements
meant for expansion of ongoing Schemes and launching of many new Schemes, the Department failed to achieve both
the physical and financial targets during 2000-01 and 2001-02. The Committee notes that a large number of new
schemes were proposed to be launched during Ninth Plan period. However, so far as their implementation is concerned,
performance has been dismal.   In the last year of the Ninth Plan, i.e.2001-02, as many as eleven new schemes were
there, out of which some were yet to be finalised due to procedural bottlenecks and in the case of others, due to late
approval, schemes were yet to take off. (Para 2.4)
            The Committee observes that as many as nineteen new schemes have been identified by the Department for
initiation during the Tenth Plan period. Scheme of CGHS Expansion in dispensaries is one of such Schemes. The
Committee is, however constrained to note that this Scheme was proposed to be launched during the Ninth Plan.  
However, for reasons unknown to the Committee, the Scheme was dropped during 1999-2000.  The Committee is
surprised to note that this Scheme is again included in the list of new schemes  to be launched during Tenth Plan.   In
contrast, fate of Schemes like 'Health for all through preventive and promotive Programme of ISMH', 'Speciality clinics
on ISMH',  ‘Indian Homoeopathy Pharmacy Council' and 'ISM Pharmacy Council’ is not known. The Committee hopes
that proper planning and preparatory exercise with regard to finalization and approval in respect of all these proposed
new schemes must have been done before making budget provision for the same in 2002-03. The Committee would like
to be enlightened in this regard.(Para 2.5)
III.       BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
            The Committee does not agree with the contention of the Secretary that  the Department is new.  It is seven years
since the Department has been created for the very specific purpose of promoting and developing indigenous Health
systems.  The Committee, therefore, feels that without  the adequate  initiative  and support of the Department, these
systems will not develop and the purpose for which the Department has been created will get defeated.  The Committee,
is, therefore, of the opinion that the Department should make all out efforts to utilise the fund  earmarked for the

118th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20HRD/118threport.htm[01-07-2016 15:17:26]
purposes  for which they are meant. (Para 3.4)
IV.       AYURVEDA
            The Committee regrets to  note from the above table that the CCRAS, Jamnagar was able to utilise only Rs. 40
lakhs out of Rs. 75 lakhs provided last year. Now the Department proposes to give Rs. one crore.     The Committee 
would  like to be apprised of the reason for lesser utilization by the Institute during 2001-02. The Committee is of the
view that concerted efforts should be made for optimum utilisation of funds during 2002-03.  The Committee desires
that PG courses proposed to be commenced in NIA, Jaipur and CCRAS, Jam Nagar be started  itself. (Para 4.3)
           
            The Committee notes that in spite of a number of initiatives being taken by the Department, not much
improvement seems to have been made. This is evident by the fact that no specific action-taken reports on 160
misleading advertisements forwarded to State Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka,
Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, NCT of Delhi, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh have been received in spite of reminders
being sent to them. The Committee notes with serious concern that during 2001-02 (upto 14.2.02), 122 advertisements
were sent to the  Government of NCT of Delhi with no response forthcoming. This is indeed a sorry state of affairs. The
Committee enjoins upon the Department to vigorously pursue the matter with the concerned State Governments,
otherwise the efficacy of Ayuvedic medicines would be questioned.       The Committee would like to be apprised of the
initiatives taken and the results thereof within a period of three months. (Para 4.5)
The Committee notes that this proposal seems to have been initiated during 2000-01 and an expenditure of about
Rs.217 lakhs was incurred during 2001-02. The Committee feels that scrutiny of expression of interest may be
completed soon  and steps may be taken to establish it at the earliest. (Para 4.7)
            The Committee notes that the Department has taken adequate steps to popularise the system of  Ayurveda in
different countries.  The Committee hopes that such  initiatives will continue in  future also. (Para 4.11)
            The Committee feels that adequate steps have not been taken by the Government to provide ayurvedic treatment
facilities to the CGHS beneficiaries.  At the same time, no serious efforts are being made to strengthen the system as the
ayurvedic hospitals/centers continued to be under the Department of Health.  The Committee would, therefore,
recommend that all facilities of ayurvedic treatment should be transferred within a period of three months  to the
Department of Indian System of Medicine and Homoeopathy so as to ensure their proper management. Further, the
existing Government CGHS dispensaries/hospitals should be upgraded and private hospitals/dispensaries such as Arya
Vaidashala Kottakkal, Kerala, and its Delhi branch may also be brought under the facilities of CGHS beneficiaries.  The
Committee also feels that the Indian System of Medicine and Homoeopathy should be headed by a professional
adoctor(vaidya) at Secretary level rather than a civil servant who may not be adequately familiar with what kind of
policies need to be formulated in this area.  This will also facilitate taking decisions for cultivation of herbs which are
the basic raw-material for manufacturing  of all these medicines. (Para 4.15)
V.        HOMOEOPATHY
The Committee, however, notes that against an allocation of Rs. 4.00 Crores for NIH in 2001-02, expenditure
reported upto February,2002 is only Rs. 2.91 Crores. The Committee observes that all the proposed activities for the
year could not be activated. Like  Laboratories could not be modernised to the required level as targetted. Similarly, no
progress seems to have been made on the proposal for starting courses for Dispensers/Pharmacists/Nurses of the
Institute. What is a cause for  more serious concern  is the issue of increase of bed capacity from 60 to 100. The
Committee has been given to understand  that steps have been taken to enhance the bed capacity to 80 at the first stage
followed by 100 later. (Para 5.2)
The Committee notes that  in this connection cadre review committee had suggested creation of 44 posts in
various categories including teaching and non-teaching.  However, the Department proposes to create 47 posts.  The
Committee would like to know the reasons for creation of 3 extra posts by the Department on their own when an expert
committee has threadbare discussed the matter.  The Committee would also like to know whether these extra posts are
on the teaching side or  the non-teaching side. (Para 5.3)
VI.       UNANI
However, theCommittee regrets  to note that the Department is silent on the issue of increase in allocation and in

118th Report
